question.text: `Shubham Family Trust` donates INR 10 lakh to `Swasth Bharat Trust` (a 50% category 80G-registered NPO) during FY 2024-25. Ignoring the qualifying-limit cap and assuming the donor has adequate taxable income, how much deduction can the donor claim under Section 80G?

answer.text: INR 10,00,000 — 100% deduction since the receiving entity is 12AB-registered
Nil — Section 80G applies only to PM's National Relief Fund category

explanation.text: The Logic: 80G has two categories: 100% deduction (e.g., PM National Relief Fund, PMCARES) and 50% deduction (most private 80G-registered NPOs). `Swasth Bharat Trust` is in the 50% category, so donor's deduction = 50% of INR 10 lakh = INR 5,00,000 (before qualifying-limit cap of 10% of adjusted GTI). The Trap: 100% deduction applies only to specified funds (PMNRF, PMCARES, CM Relief, etc.) — not to private 50%-category NPOs. 20% is a fabricated rate. Nil ignores that 80G does extend to approved private NPOs at 50%. Cross-Exam Context: V-A (MF Distributor) covers donor-side 80G planning for HNIs; XXIII tests the same rate from the SE-certification side — when SIA signs the 80G receipt register check, the 50% vs 100% category is confirmed in the certificate. Assessor's Pro-Tip: During fieldwork, photograph the 80G certificate showing the explicit 50% or 100% qualifier and retain it in your working paper. If the NPO has wrongly printed '100%' on donor receipts without backing, that is a material compliance finding — flag in the SIA report.
